messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT SEV2 — GPU pool eu-west-1 saturated, autoscaler failed to add capacity. Page sent to #incidents and @alice_oncall — 1754500123

alice_oncall: I'm on it. seeing queue growth on pool-gpu-eu-1, ~98% utilization, pending queue up ~3.2k requests. ETA to ack 1m.

bob_sre: grabbing metrics. looks like autoscaler attempted scale but Kubernetes pods kept stuck in Pending due to node quota errors: 
```
Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m  default-scheduler  0/6 nodes are available: 6 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
```
Also seeing our scale-controller leader changed recently (leader lease renew fail) — leader election flapped 3x in last 10m.

carol_runtime: confirming: the autoscale controller logs show `failed to provision nodegroup: quota_exceeded`. Provider responded 429 + rate-limited in the provisioning path.

dan_prodops: provider console shows regional GPU quota at 100, we've been at 100. There were two tenant bursts that pushed usage up simultaneously. We have no spare capacity in that region.

emma_custsuccess: hearing from two customers about degraded responses in EU. one on premium plan reported 500s for embeddings. tagging @frank_eng for customer impact assessment.

frank_eng: thanks. can we migrate high-priority requests to fallback model variant in us-east temporarily? what's cross-region latency impact?

carol_runtime: we can route non-low-latency customers to us-east fallback. need config change on routing table: `route-policy: region-preference` -> add `fallback: us-east-1` for model/embedding route.

alice_oncall: immediate mitigations proposed: 1) Evict low-priority batch jobs in eu pool (runbook step). 2) Temporarily reroute non-SLA traffic to us-east fallback. 3) Open capacity request with provider and increase quota. 4) Manually scale up a smaller GPU flavor in eu if possible. Which order?

bob_sre: do 1 then 2 in parallel. eviction reduces queue and gives breathing room. 3 is slow (provider). 4 depends on available flavors — can be quick if NBs free.

carol_runtime: eviction command ready, will run `kubectl label eviction=active` on batch namespaces then scale replica sets down. sample command: 
```
# evict low-priority
kubectl -n batch-ns scale deploy batch-worker --replicas=0
```

alice_oncall: go for it, carol. call out if we hit stuck pods.

carol_runtime: scaling batch-worker -> 0 now. logs: 1200 queue items freed (jobs moved to cold storage). queue depth down to 1.9k. :white_check_mark:

bob_sre: queue trending down, but sustained at ~1.9k. autoscaler still can't provision new nodes because provider rejects new GPUs (quota). leader flapping likely prevented the controller from retrying correctly. I can patch the controller to increase retry window and avoid lease renewal races.

alice_oncall: is there an immediate hotfix we can apply to the controller to avoid leader election churn?

bob_sre: yes, quick patch: bump leader election leaseDuration from 15s -> 60s. I can apply a rollout to the controller. small risk. would take ~3m to roll.

frank_eng: patch the controller but be cautious — if we accidentally create two controllers thinking they're leaders, double-scaling could occur. confirm prechecks.

bob_sre: prechecks run, will deploy to eu cluster only. doing rollout: `kubectl apply -f controller-vfix.yaml` now. progress: 1/1 pods updated. health checks passing.

alice_oncall: nice. while bob rolls, dan can you coordinate provider quota request? open ticket + escalate.

dan_prodops: ticket opened with provider: INC-9421. requested emergency quota increase + explanation of autoscaler misfire. they've acknowledged, SLA 2h for quota change. also exploring ad-hoc spare GPUs in other AZs.

emma_custsuccess: sent a proactive note to affected customers: "we are seeing degraded performance in eu-west-1 due to GPU capacity limits; we're routing non-SLA traffic to fallback and working to restore capacity. we'll follow up with timeline." Customers appreciated the heads-up.

carol_runtime: routing change applied: traffic for `model-embed` from free-tier -> us-east fallback. command: 
```
redwoodctl route update --route model-embed --filter tier=free --fallback-region us-east-1
```
Traffic split ~25% to us-east. Observed: eu queue depth drops further to 800 over 12m.

alice_oncall: any sign of evicted pods or stuck pods?

carol_runtime: one stuck pod in `gpu-operator` namespace due to image pull throttling, restarted it: `kubectl delete pod gpu-operator-7f9d` -> new pod in Running. good.

bob_sre: after controller lease bump, leader election stabilized, controller started reattempting provisioning logic, but provider quota still limits new nodes. Once quota grants, controller will provision.

dan_prodops: provider responded to ticket: temporary +25 GPUs in eu-west-1 for next 3 hours, request to use existing node flavors only. They've provisioned 10 so far (showing as available), will continue provisioning remainder in next 10m.

alice_oncall: start gradual scale up of nodegroup using available 10 GPUs. do not auto-scale beyond that until provider confirms full increase.

carol_runtime: scaling nodegroup `eu-gpu-pool` +10 now. `kubectl get nodes` shows 4 new nodes with GPUs joining. kube-scheduler placing Pending pods onto them, several pods transitioned to Running. queue starts to drain faster.

frank_eng: tracking customer errors — premium customers error rate down from 6% -> 1.2% after routing + scale. still monitoring.

gina_security: quick note — no evidence of any auth or config tampering, this looks capacity/rate related. I'll follow-up in postmortem with any needed RACI changes.

alice_oncall: timeline recap for postmortem: 
- 1754500123 incident triggered by autoscale fail + regional quota limit + leader election churn.
- 1754500140 batch eviction started.
- 1754500250 routing to fallback applied.
- 1754500400 leader election lease bump deployed.
- 1754500600 provider emergency quota partially granted (10/25).
- 1754500820 manual nodegroup scaled +10.
- 1754501200 queue below threshold, incident de-escalated to monitoring.

bob_sre: root causes (preliminary): 
1) quota exhaustion in eu-west-1 due to overlapping tenant bursts.
2) autoscaler didn't recover quickly because controller leader leases were too short and flapped under load.
3) provider rate-limit + quota behavior caused 429/Provision errors without adequate retry/backoff in our provisioning path.

frank_eng: impact: several customers saw elevated latencies and 500s on embeddings for ~40min, premium customers had partial failures but core SLA met after reroute. Estimated ~0.2% request loss for premium in that window.

emma_custsuccess: customers in ticket asked for postmortem and timeline. I'll coordinate customer-facing summary once we have action items.

alice_oncall: action items (owners + ETA): 
- Dan: formal quota increase request and long-term quota baseline review for eu-west-1. ETA 72h.
- Bob: merge leader-election lease bump permanently and add canary test to simulate election flapping. ETA 48h.
- Carol: add automated eviction policy for batch namespaces when pool saturation >85%. ETA 7d.
- Frank: add routing rule automation so non-SLA fallback is automatic at 75% pool utilization. ETA 5d.
- Gina: update incident checklist to include quota/provider escalation matrix. ETA 3d.
- Alice: run a postmortem writeup and schedule blameless review. ETA 2d.

bob_sre: small follow-up: need to instrument our provisioning path to surface 429 vs quota_exceeded clearly in telemetry. I'll add metric `provision.fail_reason` tag. ETA 3d.

carol_runtime: I'll open a PR for the eviction playbook and add the `kubectl` commands + safety checks. linking PR in thread.

dan_prodops: provider confirmed the remaining GPUs will be ready in 45m. planning a request to increase baseline quota by 50% for seasonality due to recent growth.

alice_oncall: incident moving to monitoring. thanks everyone for quick response. final note: avoid customer-facing deep technical details — give them concise timeline + mitigations.

emma_custsuccess: will draft customer note after postmortem.

frank_eng: adding retrospective note: run a scheduled chaos test for leader election under load. we learned this is brittle.

gina_security: tagging security triage not required, but keep me in loop for postmortem distribution.

alice_oncall: closing thread in 2h if no regressions. :checkered_flag: 

incident-bot: INCIDENT_UPDATE — incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. incident severity reduced to SEV3 at 1754501886.
